title: What Is Claude?
description: Meet Claude — Anthropic's AI assistant designed to be helpful, harmless, and honest. Learn what it is, what it can do, and why it was built differently from other AI tools.

data.text: Claude is an AI assistant created by Anthropic, a company founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers. Unlike many AI assistants that are built primarily to be engaging or to drive engagement metrics, Claude was designed with a specific priority: to be helpful, harmless, and honest. This is not just a marketing tagline — it is the core principle behind every technical decision Anthropic makes.

Claude is a general-purpose AI assistant accessible through a web interface, mobile apps, and an API. In plain language: you type or speak a request, and Claude responds with text, code, analysis, or structured content. It can read documents, write essays, debug code, analyze data, and hold long, nuanced conversations.

data.title: What makes Claude distinct
data.text: Claude's most talked-about feature is its large context window — up to 200,000 tokens, roughly 150,000 words. That means Claude can read an entire book or a large codebase in a single conversation and reference it accurately throughout. This is one of its biggest advantages over many competing assistants.

data.title: Core things Claude can help with:
items: Writing and editing long-form text (essays, reports, documentation)
Analyzing and summarizing uploaded documents and files
Writing, reviewing, and explaining code in many languages
Answering questions with nuance and careful reasoning
Creating interactive artifacts (code, visualizations, web components)

data.title: Honest limitations to be aware of from the start:
items: Generate images or video (Claude is text-focused)
Access the live internet by default in the free tier
Execute code directly in the chat interface (Artifacts can render some code)
Guarantee factual accuracy — always verify important claims

terms.definition: The underlying technology that powers Claude — a neural network trained on vast amounts of text data.
The amount of text Claude can 'remember' in a single conversation. Claude's context window is notably large — up to 200,000 tokens.
A piece of a word that the model processes. Roughly 1,000 tokens equals 750 words.
Application Programming Interface — a way for developers to send requests to Claude programmatically and receive responses.

data.title: Real-world Claude use cases
data.content: A marketing manager uses Claude to draft a 5-page annual report. A student uses Claude to summarize a 200-page textbook PDF and generate study guides. A software engineer uses Claude to review a 10,000-line codebase and explain how authentication works. All of these are possible because of Claude's large context window and careful instruction-following.

data.title: In this lesson you learned
points: Claude is an AI assistant built by Anthropic with a focus on safety and helpfulness
Its standout technical feature is a 200,000-token context window
Claude excels at writing, analysis, code, and long-document understanding
Claude cannot generate images or browse the web in its free tier

cards.title: Claude
cards.description: Built by Anthropic. Strength: long-context reasoning, careful instruction-following, large context window (200k tokens). Best for: document analysis, long-form writing, nuanced reasoning.

cards.title: ChatGPT
cards.description: Built by OpenAI. Strength: plugin ecosystem, browsing, code interpreter, wide adoption. Best for: research, web browsing, coding with built-in tools.

cards.title: Gemini
cards.description: Built by Google. Strength: multimodal understanding, Google Workspace integration, large context. Best for: image analysis, Workspace users, research with Google Search.

data.title: More real-world Claude use cases
data.content:
A technical writer uses Claude to analyze a 300-page API reference and generate a 10-page getting-started guide.

A startup founder uses Claude to review a 40-page pitch deck and suggest improvements for investor clarity.

A researcher uses Claude to compare 15 research papers and synthesize the key disagreements in the field.

All of these work well because of Claude's ability to hold large documents in context and reason across them carefully.
